what: Illinois Tool Works makes industrial products through 88 decentralised divisions: car parts, commercial food equipment, welding gear, testing instruments, specialty adhesives and packaging materials.
customers: Carmakers, restaurants and food retailers, construction firms, electronics manufacturers and industrial buyers worldwide.
money: fasteners and components built into vehicles
commercial ovens, mixers, dishwashers and service
welding equipment, adhesives, construction fasteners and specialty products
moat: Thousands of patented, specified components sold at good margins into applications where the part is cheap but failure is expensive.
risks: Revenue has been flat for three years as industrial demand stalled
Car production volumes are falling in Europe and North America
Construction activity depends on interest rates
Growth depends on end markets it cannot influence
opportunities: Return on invested capital near 27% and operating margins near 26% are among the best in industry
Its decentralised model lets divisions raise prices quickly when costs rise
Consistent cash generation funds dividends raised for decades and steady buybacks
watch: Organic revenue growth, which has been the weak point, by segment.
